principle: AUREN owns orchestration semantics; providers supply inference and native capabilities

chatgpt.important: Do not model ordinary ChatGPT chat as a local subprocess provider. Use Codex in ChatGPT, an approved MCP app, or the API when execution is required.

chatgpt_web.current_gap: AUREN has no published ChatGPT plugin and no remote Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint. The existing local stdio capability cannot be connected directly to ChatGPT web.
next_steps: Deploy an authenticated remote MCP endpoint or Secure MCP Tunnel bridge.
Expose narrowly scoped tools with read/write separation and approval metadata.
Package the AUREN skill and MCP app as a ChatGPT plugin; test on supported workspace plans.

chatgpt_desktop_codex.current_gap: Repository guidance and skills exist, but no AUREN plugin is published in the ChatGPT/Codex universal directory and no desktop live conformance run is recorded.
next_steps: Install the AUREN skill in the supported project or user skill directory.
Register the AUREN MCP server in Codex settings.
Package and publish a plugin if ChatGPT Chat/Work distribution is required.

codex_cli.current_gap: The provider conformance harness supports a read-only CLI probe, but no successful live probe from this audit environment is recorded.
next_steps: Install Codex CLI and authenticate.
Run the static provider conformance suite, then the opt-in read-only live probe.
Verify MCP discovery and exact-head CI behavior in a disposable repository.

codex_app.current_gap: The same repo instructions and skills are available, but app-specific MCP registration and end-to-end behavior are not live tested.
next_steps: Install the AUREN skill in the project or user skill directory.
Add MCP server through Codex app settings and verify tool discovery.
Run a read-only repository task followed by a sandboxed change and exact-head verification.

claude_chat_web.current_gap: Claude chat is not Claude Code. It does not inherit local CLAUDE.md, local skills, or local shell access just because the repository contains them.
next_steps: Use Claude Code for repository execution.
For chat-only use, attach the required artifacts and keep execution in AUREN CLI.
If remote tool use is enabled, connect a separately deployed authenticated MCP service.

claude_code_cli.current_gap: Repository integration is present; provider CLI execution and permission-mode compatibility still need live checks against the installed Claude Code version.
next_steps: Install Claude Code and the AUREN plugin or skill.
Verify /mcp and plugin hook discovery.
Run the opt-in read-only probe, then a sandboxed disposable-repo acceptance run.

mechanisms: Claude Desktop Code tab / Claude Code
claude_desktop.current_gap: The plugin and skill are packaged, but Desktop-specific plugin installation and the Code tab workflow are not verified here. Ordinary Claude chat remains chat-only.
next_steps: Use the Code tab / Claude Code experience, not ordinary chat, for repository execution.
Install the AUREN plugin and confirm MCP server status.
Run a read-only smoke test and verify the tool cannot bypass AUREN gates.

claude_vscode.current_gap: No automated VS Code extension smoke test or editor-specific setup validation is in CI.
next_steps: Install the official Claude Code VS Code extension.
Open the AUREN repository as the workspace and verify CLAUDE.md and skill discovery.
Check MCP status and run a read-only test before enabling write actions.

mechanisms: GitHub Copilot MCP support in Visual Studio
visual_studio_ide.current_gap: Visual Studio can host MCP through GitHub Copilot, but AUREN has no dedicated Visual Studio extension and no live Visual Studio connection/authentication test.
next_steps: Connect the deployed AUREN endpoint using the Visual Studio Copilot MCP configuration supported by the installed version.
Verify OAuth sign-in, tool visibility, tool approvals and cancellation in a disposable repository.
Keep Visual Studio distinct from the Claude Code VS Code extension.

gemini_cli.current_gap: AUREN documentation pointed the Gemini MCP command at agency_mcp.py, which is a protocol helper rather than the stdio server. The correct stdio entry point is portable/chat_capability.py.
next_steps: Use the corrected portable/chat_capability.py stdio entry point.
Install/link the AUREN skill and verify /skills list and /mcp list.
Add Gemini headless JSONL parsing and live conformance to the provider harness.

gemini_code_assist_vscode.current_gap: Gemini CLI IDE companion and Gemini Code Assist are separate products. No dedicated Code Assist extension package or Code Assist live test is present.
next_steps: Use Gemini CLI integration in VS Code for the complete AUREN CLI/MCP path.
Validate GEMINI.md discovery for the specific Code Assist mode before relying on it.
Do not assume Gemini CLI skill/MCP configuration transfers to Code Assist.

cursor.current_gap: Cursor supports AGENTS.md, .agents/skills and MCP, but AUREN has no .cursor/rules policy file, no checked-in Cursor MCP setup, and no Cursor live conformance run.
next_steps: Add a small .cursor/rules/auren.mdc rule that delegates to AGENTS.md and the AUREN skill.
Provide an opt-in local MCP configuration using portable/chat_capability.py.
Test local and Cloud Agent skill visibility separately; local user skills are not automatically copied to cloud workers.

groq_api.current_gap: A bounded native adapter is present. Live credential acceptance, current model-ID validation, vendor-specific feature conformance, pricing, latency and outage tests remain outstanding; no provider is marked live verified.
next_steps: Set the provider API key and an explicit model ID in the deployment secret/environment configuration.
Select the provider and failover order with AUREN_REMOTE_PROVIDER_ORDER.
Run the read-only live provider conformance probe with deployment-owned credentials.
Measure cost, latency, output quality, rate limits and outage behavior before enabling production routing.
